messages:
alex: :rotating_light: heads-up — I'm rolling an emergency quota-bypass on the /v1/generate route for orgs with premium=true. Background: a bad tokenization change in the model shard caused sustained 429s for a subset of traffic at 15:02 UTC. I can flip a scoped bypass for affected orgs but want a quick runbook check before I do it.
maya: Do we have the list of affected org IDs? Can we limit to the org tag instead of route-level?
alex: I pulled a list from telemetry: orgs 8421, 8473, 8480 — all high-traffic. Easier to scope by route+org set for immediate fix.
kai: Agree limit scope. Also add a header override so downstream services still see original quota header for auditing: set X-Quota-Override: emergency-bypass.
jem: Quick note: the console rollout UX currently shows the bypass as a global toggle which is scary. If you toggle via API, please add a labeled audit note so the console shows it in the rollout timeline.
alex: Good call. I'll run the internal API (not the console) and attach a note. Plan: 1) create bypass via admin-control API 2) monitor 5xx/p95/tokens 3) remove when model rollback goes out.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-317. Severity: P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-317
kai: Share the exact API call you plan to run?
alex: Using adminctl, command: 
```
adminctl toggle-bypass --route "/v1/generate" --scope org_ids=8421,8473,8480 --meta "emergency tokenizer regression" --set-header "X-Quota-Override=emergency-bypass"
```
alex: I'll run it in 30s unless objections.
maya: Before you flip, add a telemetry gate: only on the gateway edge node pool A, not global. We want to limit blast radius.
jem: Also ensure the rollback path is trivial: adminctl toggle-bypass --id <bypass-id> --disable. Document the bypass-id in the incident.
kai: I'll watch metrics: gateway 5xx, p95 lat, token_consumption rate, and quota-throttle-rate. If 5xx goes back to baseline in 5 mins, we keep it and proceed to model rollback.
alex: flipped: adminctl returned bypass-id=bb-2026-317. Tagging note: "temporary bypass for tokenizer regression; will unwind after model rollback; ops contact @kai".
ops-bot: Audit event logged: bypass-created bb-2026-317 by alex at 2812345689
maya: I see the bypass in the rollout timeline. Console now shows a temporary policy entry. Thanks for the note.
kai: Early telemetry: quota-throttle-rate for the three orgs dropped from 18% -> 1.2% within 45s. 5xx unchanged. p95 improved marginally.
jem: Next step: push canary model rollback to the shard tomorrow and schedule a controlled migration. Add an automatic fallback in the routing policy: if 5xx rises >2x baseline for 2 minutes, auto-disable bypass and route to fallback-model-v1.
alex: Good. I'll add a routing policy rule: if error_rate_pct(route="/v1/generate") > 200 then disable bypass bb-2026-317 and route->fallback-model-v1. CLI preview: 
```
adminctl routing-rule create --if "metric(error_rate, route='/v1/generate', window='2m') > baseline*2" --then "disable-bypass bb-2026-317; set-route-variant fallback-model-v1" --note "safety auto-unwind"
```
kai: One nit: make sure the rule evaluation runs in the control plane region closest to the ingress to avoid evaluation lag.
alex: will do.
ops-bot: Automation scheduled: routing-rule rr-2026-45 will evaluate every 30s.
maya: Any rollback playbook steps for the oncall? Summarize pls.
alex: Playbook snippet for oncall: 1) Check dd metrics dashboard "gateway/generate/latency" and "quota/throttle" 2) If 5xx > baseline*2 for 5m, run `adminctl routing-rule disable rr-2026-45` then `adminctl disable-bypass bb-2026-317` 3) Run model rollback via modelctl: `modelctl rollback shard=shard-7 to=stable-2026-03` 4) Post incident note and keep bypass disabled for 1 hour after rollback.
jem: Add step 0: notify billing/sales for affected premium orgs so they don't hit unexpected quota meters.
kai: I'll stay on watch for 30m. Thanks for the quick action.
alex: Closing loop: leaving the bypass active until model rollback finishes; will post final status. :white_check_mark:
